lines: adonné à toute eſpece de larrecins, & af-
Les teſmoins raportoyent qu'iceluy du Tilh eſtoit
couſtumier iurer teſte, corps, ſang & playes de noſtre
Seigneur: ce que vulgairement on appelle Blaſphemer:
qui n'eſt autre choſe, ſelon l'expoſition des Theologiés,
choſes à Dieu, qui ne luy conuiennent point: ou bien
detraire de ce que luy appartient {a}. combien qu'à la ve-
rité, Blaſpheme ſe doyue diffinir autrement: car laiſſant
à part l'interpretation des Hebrieux, & Cabaliſtes, qui
diſent Blaſphemer le nom de Dieu n'eſtre autre choſe,
qu'exprimer ce grand & ineffable nom, Tetragramma
ton (qui ne ſe doit pronõcer ou eſcrire) Par ces lettres,
& caracteres faut entendre que Blaſpheme, eſt vn nom
tiré du Grec, qui ſignifie deteſtation, iniure, meſpris, ma
ledicéce, & vitupere. Dont Blaſphemer, à parler propre
ment, eſt meſpriſer, deteſter, & contumelier Dieu, ou
ſon fils Ieſus Chriſt {b}, les prouoquant d'opprobres &
iniures {c}. Ainſi quãd les Iuifs iettoient des pierres cõtre
noſtre Sauueur Ieſus-chriſt, ils diſoiẽt le lapider, nõ pas
pour bonnes œuures (comme le Seigneur iuſtemẽt ſe
plaignoit:) mais pour Blaſpheme {d}. Et tels Blaſphema-
teurs, par la loy anciéne eſtoient lapidez du peuple {e} de
laquelle nos cõſtitutiõs ciuiles eſpuiſées, condẽnent les
Blaſphemateurs à mort: ce que deuroit eſtre religieu-
ſement gardé: & (cõme dit ſainct Gregoire) ſans vſer de
miſericorde aucune {f}: pourueu toutesfois qu'ils ſoient
couſtumiers & endurcis à ce faire {g}. Autremẽt pour vne,
deux & trois fois, la loy ne les fait pas mourir (ne voulãt
tirer à peine de mort trop facilement vn gliſſement, &
lubricité de langage {h}:) mais les puniſt extraordinaire-
mẽt, ſelon la qualité des perſonnes, & autres circonſtan
ces obſeruées: le tout remis à l'arbitre du iuge {i}: d'autãt
que la loy peſe, tels blaſphemes inaccouſtumez, proce-
der plus de quelque paſſion, legereté d'eſprit, ou mau

uncertain.note: the mark over the middle vowel of 'maledicéce' (ma- on the previous line) reads as an acute é, but could be the tilde this print uses elsewhere for an omitted n, giving 'maledicẽce'. Transcribed literally as printed; not re-cropped, per the single-pass rule.

uncertain.text: teurs, par la loy anciéne eſtoient lapidez du peuple {e} de
uncertain.note: 'anciéne' for 'ancienne' (single n where two are expected); no tilde is visible over the é, so this is transcribed as printed, sic.

uncertain.text: que la loy peſe, tels blaſphemes inaccouſtumez, proce-
uncertain.note: a faint mark sits over the e of 'peſe'; the word (from 'peſer', to weigh) has no reason to carry the nasal tilde used elsewhere on this page, so the mark is read as ink noise rather than a diacritic and 'peſe' is transcribed plain.

the first two lines of note a (the author name before 'au fin. de maled.') are not confidently legible at native strip resolution; best literal reading given with [?] for the illegible letters. Escalate for reconciler check against the other reader's read.

the key letter of this note reads more like an italic 'h' than 'b' in the cursive hand, but it is the second note on the page (right after key a) and the body's second marker is {b} (on 'Chriſt'), so it is keyed 'b' by position; the glyph itself is ambiguous between b and h.
'de religioſ' ends its line with no visible period or hyphen, possibly an abbreviation for 'religioſis'; the numeral 'xxiiij' vs 'xiiij' is hard to distinguish at this resolution.

literal reading is 'c. xiiij.' (Leviticus 14), but the biblical passage on stoning blasphemers is Leviticus 24 (matching key c's citation on this same page); the x-count is genuinely hard to read at this resolution, as on p056's comparable Pliny citation.

uncertain.text: c reos ſan- / guinis. C. xxiij. / q. v.
uncertain.note: the numeral after 'guinis.' reads as 'C. xxiij.' but could be 'c. xiij.'; 'q. v.' is clear.
compressed abbreviation at the head of note g; the exact letters between 'Parag' and 'fin' are unclear at this resolution, read as 'Parag. fin.'

could not confidently locate a key-letter glyph 'i' before 'Les interpretes en la loy. v.'; this citation and the following one ('C. de reb. cre. P. item ſi quis poſtulante. de actio.') are grouped as note i by elimination, since the body's last marker {i} would otherwise have no note. The boundary between h's note and i's note is uncertain; h's note may instead extend to include the 'Les interpretes' line.
a mark over the c of this word could not be identified at this resolution; read as plain 'actio.'
